# Feedback

`@kerfjs/ui:feedback` · Kerf UI · CSS composition · Feedback

## When to use

Banners, empty states, and labeled progress.

- Compose persistent status, empty/busy content, and compact loading feedback.

**Not when:**

- Do not collapse different message lifetimes or urgency into one visual treatment.

**Alternatives:**

- [StateBanner](./state-banner.md) (nearest)
- [EmptyState](./empty-state.md) (nearest)
- [Callout](./wa-callout.md) (prefer-over)
- [Toast](./wa-toast.md) (prefer-over)

## Imports

- Nothing to import: this is a reference composition.
- Declared side effects: css.

## Props

No props: this entry has no JavaScript API.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- banner
- empty
- busy
- spinner

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.
- Built from: [StateBanner](./state-banner.md), [EmptyState](./empty-state.md), [LoadingSpinner](./loading-spinner.md).

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** state mapping; message lifetime; recovery policy.

No wiring helper.

## Geometry

Margin: child · border: child · padding: child (layout role: feedback). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

## Accessibility

- Choose polite status versus assertive alert deliberately.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
